scope: Implement actual managed Jupiter Swap v2 request/order/signing/execute transport and consumer quantities. Tests replace HTTP/RPC and directly bind a detached signer with public synthetic fixture keys; no operator key, provider API request, wallet RPC, real order, runtime launch or active model/policy change.
user_objective: Preserve requested exact 0.1 SOL paper sizing and uncapped extreme-runner exits. Use the actual selected managed order rather than an unrelated Metis route to assess execution risk, preserving RFQ/Dflow/OKX availability without bypassing original amount, wallet, impact, slippage or fee-reserve checks. This is not evidence of winning signals or captured profits.
findings: Managed defaults still used Ultra v1, although current primary documentation identifies Swap v2 as its successor.

Order inputs coerced amounts/slippage and accepted transaction/requestId without binding original mints, amount, taker, actual signer layout, supported version, output protection, fee payer or validity metadata.
Execution accepted missing/unknown success status and unrelated signatures/quantities. The buyer consumed order.outAmount, an estimate, rather than the actual provider-reported wallet output.
A separate Metis precheck could veto a valid managed RFQ/Dflow/OKX winner; consumers selected managed mode merely from API-key presence despite an explicit disable flag.
Managed execute POST was not retained as an owned execution worker through repeated cancellation, unlike repaired local signing.

implementation.current_protocol: Use Swap v2 order/execute defaults in source and .env.example. Normalize known api.jup.ag Ultra v1 overrides to current paths without editing personal .env. Reject foreign/insecure/credentialed/query-bearing endpoint overrides before any HTTP and disable GET/POST redirects; API credentials remain scoped to the official HTTPS host. Explicitly request supported transaction version0; do not pretend installed SDK supports v1.
implementation.request_bound_order: Validate canonical public addresses, distinct original mints, exact positive integer uint64 input, explicit ExactIn/slippage0..10000, supported router/mode, original output threshold and current v2 signed percentage-point impact. Validate taker as a required original v0 signer, packet bounds, existing non-placeholder signature validity, original fee-payer layout, strict network/rent estimates and sponsorship, requested wallet reserve, token-fee metadata and aggregator/RFQ validity. Preserve nullable metadata only where it cannot authorize unknown nonzero charges. No unrelated Metis gate is imposed on managed routing.
implementation.signing: Use existing pure common-SDK signing in an owned worker. Verify original message, wallet signature/index and all unchanged co-signatures before execute. Recheck RFQ expiry after signing. Freeze canonical original order/request digests, message digest and public wallet-signature provenance. Unsigned instruction semantic intent and independently measured market-asof remain unverified.
implementation.one_owned_execute: Execute one original signed packet/requestId/positive validity height on an HTTP loop entirely contained in an owned executor invocation. Omit absent/zero RFQ height instead of sending an already-expired aggregator nonce; preserve its checked original timestamp expiry. Repeated caller cancellation joins the POST worker, retains original durable owner and propagates cancellation only after settlement. No rebuild, re-sign, POST retry or uncertain fallback is added. A transport/status/JSON/response failure after POST is always SwapSubmissionUncertain, even when it resembles a preparation error.
implementation.checked_response: Require explicit Success/code0, original-signature equality when present before execute, cryptographic verification against the original fee-payer key and exact original message for every returned first signature, positive reported slot, exact original total input, positive uint64 wallet/route quantities, minimum original output and compatible fee deductions. Preserve all four quantities separately. A provider-added sponsor signature can be verified without knowing it before execute; distinguish first_signature_present_before_execute from first_signature_bound and never invent the earlier signature. All independently measured chain/wallet/content proofs remain false and require reconciliation.
implementation.consumers: Buyer uses checked execute wallet-output units, not quoted units; carries the receipt with provider-only/financially-unverified flags. Apply original impact and existing wallet reserve to the selected order before signing. Proved preparation failures become durable NO_JUP_ORDER no-fill without GMGN purchase fallback. Seller permits existing liquidity-gated canonical-mint fallback only before any execute POST. Respect explicit managed/legacy disable flags despite API-key presence.
implementation.unchanged: No runtime launch, personal environment/key, active artifact, policy, live activation, trading size or new take-profit ceiling. Existing primary/capital guards remain. Source-only publishing checkout is not provisioned with credentials, a virtual environment or runtime DB.

Provider-reported confirmed slot/quantities are explicitly not an independent wallet proof. Existing configured HTTP timeouts and production latency, including serial monitor waiting on its own position's provider, remain to be validated. Owned waits cannot guarantee an OS shutdown deadline for a hung worker.
